title: Coherence of comparison maps normalized on an immersion image
statement:
Let schemes be quasi-compact and locally Noetherian, with small pro-etale sites [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For each coefficient label $r$ give a cartesian system of commutative ring sheaves $R_X^r$, meaning coherent identifications $a^{-1}R_X^r=R_S^r$ for every immersion $a:S\hookrightarrow X$. Write $D(X,r)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_X^r))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the exact extensions $E_a^r=a_{!,r}$, restriction isomorphisms $a_r^*E_a^r\cong1$, and factorization/composition maps $\gamma^r_{a,b}:E_a^rE_b^r\cong E_{ab}^r$ of [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence].

Suppose functors $F_X^{rs}:D(X,r)\to D(X,s)$ have coherent isomorphisms $q_a^{rs}:a_s^*F_X^{rs}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_S^{rs}a_r^*$, respecting identity and composition. For open and closed immersions suppose isomorphisms $d_a^{rs}:F_X^{rs}E_a^r\xrightarrow{\sim}E_a^sF_S^{rs}$ are given whose restriction is $q_a^{rs}$ under $a^*E_a\cong1$. For a factorization $a=vc$ with $c$ closed and $v$ open, form $d_a=(E_v^s d_c)\circ(d_v E_c^r)$, inserting $\gamma$. These composites are independent of factorization, including comparison with open-then-closed factorizations, and satisfy
$$d_{ab}\circ F_X^{rs}(\gamma^r_{a,b})=\gamma^s_{a,b}F_T^{rs}\circ(E_a^s d_b)\circ(d_aE_b^r)$$
for $b:T\hookrightarrow S$.

If also natural isomorphisms $t_X:F_X^{st}F_X^{rs}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_X^{rt}$ are given and satisfy
$$q_a^{rt}\circ(a_t^*t_X)=(t_Sa_r^*)\circ F_S^{st}(q_a^{rs})\circ(q_a^{st}F_X^{rs}),$$
then the assembled comparisons satisfy
$$E_a^t(t_SM)\circ d_a^{st}(F_S^{rs}M)\circ F_X^{st}(d_a^{rs}M)=d_a^{rt}(M)\circ t_X(E_a^rM).$$
This is conditional coherence for already given comparisons; it asserts no existence of scalar-extension or pullback comparisons.

proof.text:
Put $L_a^r=a_r^*$ and let $\rho_a^r:L_a^rE_a^r\cong1$ be the cited restriction isomorphism. Quasi-compact plus locally Noetherian is its Noetherian hypothesis, and cartesian rings supply every inverse-image coefficient. Insert coherent restriction compositors throughout. Call $h_a$ normalized when
$$\rho_a^sF_S^{rs}\circ L_a^s(h_a)=F_S^{rs}(\rho_a^r)\circ(q_a^{rs}E_a^r).\tag{N}$$
The supplied open and closed maps satisfy (N); normalized extension compositors satisfy (G) of the binary-restriction lemma. The generic predicates [def-sfb-immersion-comparison-normalized, def-sfb-immersion-comparison-composition] name these exact equations before specializing to derived categories. For (G), use the module extension-normalization law, the supplied termwise characterizations of derived restriction and gamma, and exact-functor derived composition coherence. Transport along the cartesian coefficient equality. The identity-factorization equation in the termwise bridge is the existing public Functor.mapDerivedCategoryIdIso_hom_app_Q_obj, imported from Sheaf.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.ExactRestrictionComposition; no duplicate identity-factorization theorem is introduced.

Restriction detects equality between isomorphic extension images: for $u:A\cong E_a^sP$, $v:B\cong E_a^sQ$, equal restrictions of $f,g:A\to B$ imply equal restrictions of $vfu^{-1},vgu^{-1}$. Injectivity of the cited Hom bijection gives $f=g$. Thus an existing comparison isomorphism $h_0:F_X^{rs}E_a^rM\cong E_a^sF_S^{rs}M$ makes a comparison with prescribed (N) unique (take $u=h_0,v=1$). Componentwise this gives uniqueness of natural transformations; global faithfulness or support preservation of $F$ is unnecessary.

For $a=vc$, $c$ closed and $v$ open, set
$$d_a=\gamma_{v,c}^sF_S^{rs}\circ(E_v^sd_c)\circ(d_vE_c^r)\circ F_X^{rs}((\gamma_{v,c}^r)^{-1}).$$
Apply the binary-restriction lemma to the supplied normalized $d_v,d_c$: $d_a$ is a normalized isomorphism. The extension theorem identifies every other closed-then-open presentation with $E_a$, restricting to the identity. Its constructed comparison has the same (N), hence equals $d_a$ by Step 2. For a supplied $a=iu$, $u$ open and $i$ closed, the theorem supplies the normalized $\gamma_{i,u}$; apply the same binary lemma and uniqueness. Supplied maps for already open or closed $a$ also agree by (N) and uniqueness.

For arbitrary composable $a,b$, the binary-restriction lemma applied to the constructed normalized $d_a,d_b$ makes
$$\widetilde d_{ab}=\gamma_{a,b}^sF_T^{rs}\circ(E_a^sd_b)\circ(d_aE_b^r)\circ F_X^{rs}((\gamma_{a,b}^r)^{-1})$$
normalized. It and $d_{ab}$ have identical source and target. Step 2 gives equality; precompose by $F_X^{rs}(\gamma_{a,b}^r)$ to obtain the stated immersion-composition equation.

Fix a compatible triple $r,s,t$, an immersion $a$, and $M$. The tower-restriction lemma applies with the constructed normalized comparisons and the assumed $q/t$ square; its (L) gives equal restrictions of the two tower paths $h_L,h_R$. Their source is isomorphic to $E_a^t(F_S^{st}F_S^{rs}M)$ via $d_a^{st}(F_S^{rs}M)\circ F_X^{st}(d_a^{rs}(M))$, and their target is $E_a^tF_S^{rt}M$. The Hom bijection and Step 2 therefore give $h_L=h_R$, naturally in $M$. The objects on $S$ may differ; only membership up to isomorphism in the extension image is needed.
